title: Group rings over Z[(1+i)/2] of G(m,p,n) and its mystic partner are isomorphic for n>=1, even m>=2 and p dividing m
author: Yuri Bazlov; Arkady Berenstein
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs an explicit automorphism of the monomial-group algebra from parity-dependent root-system cocycles and finite diagonal idempotent factors. Restricting its parameter to i preserves the specified integral coefficient ring and sends reflection generators to combinations of mystic generators, proving a group-ring isomorphism even when the underlying groups are not isomorphic.
source_version: Official SIGMA 10 (2014) article 040, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2014.040; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.note: Complete MainTheorem2.8 and the explicit J_c construction in Proposition2.3/Lemmas3.2-3.4 read, with the mystic-partner description MainTheorem2.5 and full faithfulness/Dedekind argument in Appendix4.1-4.3. G=G(m,p,n),C orderm,C-prime orderm/p and mu(G)={tw in C^n semidirect S_n:det(tw) in C-prime}. The coefficient ring is exactly R=Z[(1+i)/2], and J_i(si)=((1+i)/2)sigma_i+((1-i)/2)sigma_i inverse, with J_i fixing the common diagonal subgroup. The inverse automorphism is explicitly J_(i inverse). No invariant-ring, group-isomorphism classification or odd-m extension is selected. Claim3.1 cocycle identities are explicit routine root-system identities, not an omitted construction.

statement_scope: Full MainTheorem2.8 with MainTheorem2.5 hypotheses n>=1,m>=2 even,p a positive divisor ofm: R G(m,p,n) is isomorphic to R mu(G) for R=Z[(1+i)/2], hence the complex group rings are isomorphic. This does not assert the groups themselves are isomorphic or an integral-Z group-ring isomorphism.
source_boundary_note: The complete original Main Theorem 2.8 over R=Z[(1+i)/2] is retained with the explicit J_c automorphism, cocycle/product identities, action comparison, mystic-partner description and full faithful-action/Dedekind Appendix argument required by the construction. The selected assumptions are n>=1, even m>=2 and p dividing m. J_i fixes the common diagonal subgroup and sends each symmetric transposition to the exact displayed linear combination of sigma_i and its inverse; inverse J_(i inverse) is explicitly constructed. The cocycle identities are the author bounded routine root-system checks after their displayed formula. No group-isomorphism classification, invariant-ring theorem or odd-m extension is selected.
